title: Structural Isomorphism: Cross-domain SOC validation dataset and pipeline (v1.0)
description: A single fixed analysis pipeline applied unchanged to thirteen independent empirical systems plus four synthetic non-SOC null controls, to test cross-domain self-organized criticality (SOC) universality claims. The pipeline (soc-pipeline, MIT, ~1,595 LOC across fit / b-value / Omori-Utsu / Vuong lognormal-vs-exponential LR / bootstrap / universal collapse / null-control modules; legacy entry-point v4/lib/soc_pipeline.py, 339-line shim) implements Clauset-Shalizi-Newman 2009 maximum-likelihood power-law estimation with KS-driven x_min selection, likelihood-ratio comparison against lognormal and exponential alternatives, and Omori-Utsu temporal decay stacking. Real-system coverage: USGS earthquakes, S&P 500 daily returns, three DeFi lending protocols (Aave V2, Compound V2, MakerDAO), mouse-cortex neural avalanches, solar flares, wildfires, power-grid disturbances, GitHub event cascades, Reddit cascades, CVE vulnerabilities, Wikipedia views, and bank failures. Four synthetic nulls (folded normal, exponential, Poisson inter-arrival, Poisson Omori) are correctly rejected, ruling out the trivial failure mode 'fits everything as a power law'. Includes the B1/B3 multi-model LLM ensemble critic over a 21-candidate universality-class taxonomy (B3 taxonomy v2), per-system raw data + fit results, manifest with SHA-256 checksums, and full reproducibility instructions.
references: Clauset A., Shalizi C. R., Newman M. E. J. (2009). Power-law distributions in empirical data. SIAM Review 51(4), 661-703.
Bak P., Tang C., Wiesenfeld K. (1987). Self-organized criticality: an explanation of 1/f noise. Phys. Rev. Lett. 59, 381.
Beggs J. M., Plenz D. (2003). Neuronal avalanches in neocortical circuits. J. Neurosci. 23, 11167.
notes: Companion preprint: C1 unified five-system SOC paper (Phase 1-5 synthesis); sibling thirteen-system manuscript at paper/v0-unified-pipeline-2026-05-13.md.
